changes.before: The baseline spring scales are 1 and 2 in the prescribed model, without chemical fitting.
changes.after: The baseline spring scales 1 and 2 are relative numerical multipliers \(s\) of the retained unit-spring matrix, without chemical fitting or an assigned physical force-constant calibration. In the code's convention, \(K_{\rm unit}=\sum_e g_e g_e^T\) over all cutoff-selected baseline edges, where each Cartesian distance-gradient column places \((x_i-x_j)/\lVert x_i-x_j\rVert\) at node \(i\), its negative at node \(j\), and zeros elsewhere. Coordinates and cutoffs are in angstroms; dividing by the edge length normalises the direction, rather than assigning a physical spring constant. The full baseline is scaled as \(sK_{\rm unit}\). The earlier stiffening calculation expresses update strengths relative to that baseline through \(a/s\) and \(b/s\); the corrected restoration calculation deletes and restores unit edge matrices, with common proportional scaling of all four corners for \(s=2\). Its dimensionless determinant cycle is therefore unchanged by that common scale, as recorded, rather than representing a second calibrated molecular model.\footnote{Retained numerical conventions: \texttt{branches/branch-3/ada/check\_ligand\_enm.py} and \texttt{emmy/full\_deletion\_check.py}. No kcal/mol/angstrom-squared or other physical spring unit is inferred.}

of the Gly216 distance self-response. For this ligand-inclusive mode audit, the exact contact is chain-H Gly216 alpha carbon (CA) to chain-H residue 1501, ligand 22U atom C13: the retained selection chooses the nearest 22U heavy node to Gly216 CA. This is a coarse CA--C13 distance, not Q's Gly216 carbonyl contact or the separate N1--Gly216 N/CA/C/O intervention bundle. With \(d=(x_{\rm CA}-x_{\rm C13})/\lVert x_{\rm CA}-x_{\rm C13}\rVert\), its Cartesian gradient \(g\) has block \(+d\) at CA, \(-d\) at C13 and zero elsewhere; the code does not rescale this whole vector to unit norm. The six Euclidean rigid modes are removed by restriction to their orthogonal complement. For Cartesian-normalised internal eigenvectors \(v_k\) and positive eigenvalues \(\lambda_k\) of that unit-spring matrix, the self-response is \(g^TK^+g=\sum_k(v_k^Tg)^2/\lambda_k\); the quoted lowest-mode share divides \((v_1^Tg)^2/\lambda_1\) by that entire sum. Here \(K^+\) is the inverse on the internal subspace, zero on the rigid modes. The share is dimensionless, not an absolute contact variance or a physically calibrated force-field response. The separate protein-only audit instead chooses the nearest protein CA more than 4 angstroms from Gly216 CA; its saved contact is Gly226 CA, and it is not the contact behind the quoted ligand-inclusive fraction.\footnote{Exact saved node identities and mode fraction: \texttt{branches/branch-1/emmy/mode-audit/mode-results.json}; selection, gradient and spectral sum: \texttt{check\_modes.py} in that directory; node/parser and rigid-basis definitions: \texttt{branches/branch-1/emmy/conditioning/check\_networks.py}. These retained files are inspected without executing their calculations.}
